newsitem.title: UK: Brokers Fearnoil joins growing European gas market.
newsitem.headline: Brokers Fearnoil joins growing European gas market.

text.p: Oil brokers Fearnoil became the latest company to join the growing European natural gas market on Wednesday.
"We have had growing demand from our customers to broke natural gas and feel the timing is right," said Fearnoil managing director Dave Rapp.
"Natural gas will be complementary with our existing fuel broking."
Oil dealers in Europe see a growing trend towards energy companies trading across several inter-related markets, such as gas, oil and electricity.
Fearnoil faces competition from three other brokerage companies -- Spectron Energy UK Ltd, PVM Oil Associates Ltd and EES Group Ltd.
Currently, the European gas market is characterised by bouts of hectic trading, punctuated by periods of low liquidity.
Britain is currently the only active spot market, but other European countries such as the Netherlands, Germany and Italy are expected to partially liberalise their markets soon.
Dealers expect liquidity to build up over the next few years as demand and market liberalisation develop.
World demand for gas is set to grow 60 percent by the year 2010, according to the International Energy Agency.
European demand is about 377 billion cubic metres (bcm) a year but availability will jump by 90 bcm by 1999.
